Jonava Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kauno apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Jonava's Jewish population peaked at 3,975 (80 percent) in 1897; a distinct type of physically strong, self-reliant Jewish workman developed there through the lumber trade and railroad economy. On June 22, 1941, the day Germany invaded, a Lithuanian shoemaker murdered the city's Jewish deputy mayor with an iron rod; days later, all Jews were ordered to assemble in the city square under machine guns, though a stray bomb landing nearby caused panic and a temporary scattering. During summer 1941, 2,108 Jews were shot in the Girele grove.
